meta.title: supatripwire — Cross-Tenant Read Detection for Supabase
meta.description: supatripwire reads your Supabase project's API gateway logs and reports reads where one tenant got another tenant's rows. Nothing sits in the request path, and no row contents are read.

hero.title: Cross-Tenant Read Detection for Supabase
hero.lead: supatripwire reads your project's API gateway logs and reports reads where one tenant got another tenant's rows.

named.title: It named another tenant
named.body: The log keeps the filter every signed-in read sent. supatripwire resolves each id in it to a tenant and compares it with the caller's memberships. Rows came back: data crossed. None came back: RLS stopped an attempt.
named.more: Read more about <link>what it reports</link> in the README.

ceiling.title: More rows than they could see
ceiling.body: Filters only ever narrow. A read that saw more rows than the caller's tenants hold crossed tenants, whatever its filter said, and even with no filter at all.

outside.title: Nothing in the request path
outside.body: Logs come through the Management API, ids through a read-only role you create and grant only the id and tenant columns. No proxy, no SDK, and no row contents read.
outside.doctor: Run npx supatripwire doctor to check the setup.

terminal.check: supatripwire check reporting two reads that crossed tenants
terminal.named: A finding from check 1: the read named a tenant the user is not in
terminal.ceiling: A finding from check 2: the read saw more rows than the user's tenants hold
terminal.doctor: supatripwire doctor confirming the read-only role sees every row
